content: Autoimmune type 1 diabetes constitutes approximately 5-10% of all diabetes cases. This condition arises due to the immune system-mediated destruction of pancreatic β-cells, which results in a deficiency of insulin production. Genetic predisposition plays a significant role in the development of type 1 diabetes, with specific human leukocyte antigen (HLA) haplotypes, such as HLA-DR and HLA-DQ, being strongly associated with increased susceptibility. High-risk alleles include DRB10301 and DQB10201 (commonly referred to as DR3-DQ2) as well as DRB10401 and DQB10302 (known as DR4-DQ8). The presence of autoantibodies can be detected through specific testing, which is particularly useful in identifying individuals at risk, especially those with a family history of autoimmune diseases.
